cohort: The study analyzed live births occurring in SUS childbirth care establishments in Sao Paulo State in 2016.
finding: Less urbanized regions showed significantly higher cesarean section rates than metropolitan and highly urbanized regions, and public administration establishments had significantly lower rates than nonprofit administration maternity hospitals.
mod_finding: The cesarean section rate in SUS childbirth care establishments was 50.5%, with less urbanized regions showing significantly higher rates and public administration establishments having lower rates compared to nonprofit entities, particularly in metropolitan regions.
